latestTerminalSummary:
EFFECTIVE_MODEL: opencode/space-bunny-free (settings: variant=max, runtimeMode: full-access, interactionMode: plan/read-only | evidence: requested = user-authorized "OpenCode SpaceBunny variant=max"; configured = harness-declared `opencode/space-bunny-free` in runtime-info with Plan mode active; served identity UNVERIFIED — no model banner observed in-session, so no verified-diversity claim is made)

VERDICT:         changes_required

BLOCKERS:
1. **`tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py:1535` — `agents_dir = Path("skill_lens/registry/agents")` locates the registry by pytest process CWD, not by the package under test.**
   - **Problem:** this is the only CWD-relative registry lookup in the entire suite (`tests/conftest.py` has no `chdir` fixture; `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` sets only `testpaths`/`addopts`, so nothing pins CWD). Every other registry access goes through `load_registry()` on the installed package (e.g. `tests/test_registry.py:32`) — so this is introduced by this delta, not house style. From any CWD containing a `skill_lens/registry/agents` directory the guard validates that copy and reports PASS while the repo's registry is wrong. That is the "a test that cannot fail is worse than no test" hazard AGENTS.md §4 names for new gates.
   - **Expected behaviour:** the guard must read the TOMLs shipped inside the package under test, so it fails on repo drift regardless of CWD. `agents_dir = Path(skill_lens.__file__).parent / "registry" / "agents"` (or `importlib.resources.files("skill_lens")`) — I verified both resolve to the package under test from a decoy CWD.
   - **Evidence (disposable copies outside the checkout, no repo writes):**
     - real package with `grok_bundled`'s `entry_format` deleted, test run from a decoy CWD → **1 passed** (guard blind);
     - same broken real package, run from the package root → **1 failed** at `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py:1583` (guard works);
     - decoy copy broken instead, run from the decoy → **1 failed**, proving the test reads the CWD copy.
   - **Scope of impact:** the current tree is correct and the coordinator's gate (run from the repo root) is valid evidence. Runtime format semantics are independently covered by `test_compatibility_roots_behavioral_positive_controls`, `test_explicit_directory_format_supported_forms_and_standalone_omission`, and `test_dsh_standalone_md_supported_forms_and_omissions`, all via `load_registry()`. What is uniquely lost when CWD drifts is the raw-declaration assertions and the `total_roots == 20` / per-agent root-set-and-count assertions — i.e. the only guard for "no root was added or removed to these six files".

SUGGESTIONS:
- `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py:746-748` changes `f.location` → `f.path`. This edit is not in the enumerated delta description. It is correct and behaviour-preserving: `DoctorFinding` (`skill_lens/models/doctor.py`) has `path` and no `location`, and there are zero `.location` references left in `skill_lens/` or `tests/`, so the old line survived only because `"bad_skill" in f.message` short-circuited the `or`. Name it in the change record rather than leaving it silent.
- Unpinned diagnostic-path change from the B1 fix: a **broken symlink** named `*.md` now reports `name='broken.md'` where it previously reported `'broken'` (verified before/current; `is_file=False`, canonical `broken` in both). This is the correct, consistent outcome, but it is a user-visible change in a diagnostic path with no test pinning it.
- The evidence doc records only one direction of the compatibility story. Verified against the shipped baseline (HEAD `085e28d`, which had no `entry_format` and listed root-level `*.md` unconditionally):13 (agent, root) pairs that discovered flat files at HEAD still do not — `claude_personal`, `claude_project`, `grok_global`, `qoder_global`, `qoder_project`, `windsurf_global`, `windsurf_project`, `omp_project`, `omp_project_agents`, `omp_shared_global`, plus out-of-scope `codex_project`, `codex_shared_global`, `antigravity_project_agents`. The narrowing is deliberate and primary-source-backed, so this is documentation completeness, not a defect — but it is a real behaviour change from the released tool and deserves one sentence in §6.4 alongside the six roots that *were* preserved.
- Optional: `test_entrypoint_alias_and_discovery_for_dot_md_named_directory` covers `resolve_skill`, `build_diff_report`, `run_compare`, `scan --json`, and the frozen snapshot path, but not `runner.invoke(app, ["why", ...])` or `doctor`. I verified no render/CLI/scanner layer re-derives a name from the path (`.stem` appears only at `discovery.py:670`, `parser.py:105`, `resolver.py:143`), so engine-level coverage is sound; a CLI-level assertion would be belt-and-braces.

FILES_AT_RISK:
- `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py` — BLOCKER 1 (guard bypassable by CWD). Otherwise clean: B1 and B2 guards are real and mutation-sensitive; all four coordinator mutations reproduced `control 0 / mutant 1 / restored 0` with source hashes restored.
- `skill_lens/core/resolver.py:139-144`, `skill_lens/core/discovery.py:667-672` — no risk found. All seven `entrypoint_alias` call sites pass `is_file` explicitly (lines 149, 174, 179, 181, 271, 273, 432), and `is_file` is set accurately at every `_list_entries`/`_list_recursive_entries` branch, so the removed `.md`-suffix clause only ever fired on directories. `_entry_name`'s removed clause fired only when `parse is None` and `is_file False` — exactly the B1 defect. `_document_identity` (`parser.py:105`) is unaffected because `find_skill_document` only returns `SKILL.md`/`skill.md` for directories.
- Six agent TOMLs — verified: **zero** changes to any root `id/kind/path/scope/rank/rule_id/evidence/nested_rule_id/file_rule_id/recursive/base` and zero agent-level policy changes. Only `entry_format` added and `source` repointed. All five new `source` URLs return 200; all three old URLs return 404.
- `skill_lens/registry/loader.py` — verified restored. Stripping comment lines, the current loader is byte-identical to the pre-correction loader; the only difference is the 3-line comment. The comment's claim ("some native roots remain undeclared") is accurate — `antigravity_project_agents` and `antigravity_project_agent` are still undeclared.
- `docs/validation/assessment-repairs/c/stage-c-evidence.md` — §2's stated precondition (both DSH roots resolving to `<home>/.dsh/skills` when `<home>` is a `.git` boundary) is accurate: verified that with a `.git`-bounded home and any cwd inside it, `dsh_project` (95) and `dsh_user` (70) land on the identical entrypoint path and rank-max returns 95 under both normal and permuted root order; with cwd outside a git-bounded home the collision does not occur. §1's OpenCode record matches the unchanged `opencode.toml` (native + `.agents` only; no `.claude` roots; no new roots/ranks/identity/collision/settings).
- `tests/test_session_snapshot.py` and `tests/fixtures/**` — no snapshot or golden drift; no tracked change under `tests/fixtures`.

CONCEDED:
- **My primary suspected blocker — that `entry_format = "standalone_md"` on the six "compatibility" roots breaks baseline inventory compatibility — is withdrawn.** I first reproduced it against the pre-correction Stage C tree and it looked real: all 20 roots resolved to `directory` there, and the correction adds flat-file discovery for 10 (agent, root) pairs. Re-measuring against the shipped baseline changed the answer: HEAD `085e28d` had no `entry_format` and `_list_entries` listed root-level `*.md` unconditionally, so at HEAD those six roots *did* discover flat files. The correction genuinely restores the released surface, and the claim repeated in the four TOML comments and evidence doc §6.1/§6.3/§6.4 is true. The behaviour delta against the pre-correction tree is a real expansion, but it is the intended restoration.
- **MiniMax's dead-URL objection is resolved.** Independently fetched: `code.claude.com/docs/en/skills` 200; deepseek-harness `skills.md` 200; grok-build `08-skills.md` 200; `docs.qoder.com/cli/Skills` 200; oh-my-pi `docs/skills.md` 200; `docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/skills` 301 → `docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/skills` 200. `docs.x.ai/grok-cli/skills` 404, `docs.qoder.com/skills` 404, `docs.codeium.com/windsurf/skills` 404.
- **MiniMax's OpenCode vendor-vs-implemented-root confusion is resolved.** `opencode.toml` is byte-identical to the pre-correction tree; evidence doc §1 states the vendor contract and the registry boundary separately and defers `.claude` roots to Stage D.
- **MiniMax's F07 over-claim concern is resolved.** Generic malformed/missing-description loadability remains untouched and is explicitly carried to Stage D (§6.1 #4, §6.4 items 2 and 4), and the six roots are labelled `inferred`, not vendor-proven.
- **My OpenCode B2 residual ("same agent, SAME PATH via roots at rank 95 vs 70 unpinned") is withdrawn as unresolved.** Rank-max grouping already existed at `resolver.py:265-273`; the delta adds only the regression. Verified independently of the coordinator's log: the grouping keeps `max` rank per entrypoint path, and reversing `agent.roots` genuinely reverses hit order (discovery iterates `agent.roots` in order and `_union_hits` appends), so the new test kills the first-wins mutant.
- **My OpenCode B1 is withdrawn as unresolved.** Verified end-to-end against before/current copies of the tree: pre-correction `entrypoint_alias(<dir>/shortcut.md, is_file=False)` returned `'shortcut'` while discovery already named the entry `'shortcut.md'` — the internal inconsistency — and `resolve_skill("shortcut.md")` failed while `resolve_skill("shortcut")` succeeded. Post-correction both agree on `'shortcut.md'`, and standalone files are unchanged. Also verified the two corrections do not interfere: a directory named `dirnamed.md` and a real flat `flat.md` coexist correctly under the widened `standalone_md` root.

PRIMARY-QUESTION ANSWER: Yes on both counts. The alias/type and SAME-PATH rank tests resolve B1 and B2 with no behavioural regression, and the corrected formats match both the source and the compatibility boundary — the compatibility claim held up under reproduction rather than assertion. One blocker remains, and it is guard strength rather than product behaviour: the new raw-registry guard at `tests/test_stage_c_repairs.py:1535` reads the registry through a CWD-relative path and silently passes on a broken real registry from any CWD that happens to contain `skill_lens/registry/agents`. That is a one-line, test-only fix.

Review artefacts (outside the repository, disposable): `/private/var/folders/tf/jsdyxcts6y72fs98s7wl3dfm0000gn/T/sl-review-probe-opencode`. All 335 fingerprints in the coordinator's final receipt were re-verified against the checkout as byte-identical after this review — no repository file was created, modified, or deleted.
